solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Way to get half of the characters to come forward and protest

indicators.note: to come forward is to move to the front, so this pair of letters shifts to the start of the word

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
the second two of the four letters in the word for 'way'

explanation.surface: Someone wants half the cast of a play to step up and make a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come forward' tells you to move DE, the back half of MODE, to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is short for a demonstration, a public protest march or rally.

clue.text: There's something fragrant about London's city still

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fragrant word goes round the London postcode

parts.note: balm is a sweet-smelling ointment or aromatic plant
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A perfume is said to hang over the City of London, which lies motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) is the postal district covering the City, London's financial centre. 'still' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To becalm is to make calm or still, as wind dropping leaves a ship motionless.

clue.text: Goat in alpine village

definitions.meaning: a goat is slang for a lustful man, a lecher
A ski village in the Austrian Alps

explanation.surface: A goat is spotted wandering in a mountain village.
explanation.definitionFit: Lech is short for lecher, a lustful man, which goat means figuratively; it is also a resort in Austria's Arlberg region.

clue.text: Cover bishop looking at website?

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
someone browsing a website is on the net

explanation.surface: A bishop searching online for a mitre or other head covering.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose phrase: viewing a website means being 'on (the) net'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet is a hat, or in Britain the hinged panel covering a car's engine.

clue.text: Robot has strange item of headgear

indicators.note: strange suggests things out of their usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A robot is wearing an odd hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' shuffles the letters of ROBOT HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarboosh is a brimless felt cap like a fez, worn by men in the Middle East.

clue.text: Trader in awful place, seaman reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the words are taken by how they sound

parts.note: an awful place is a hole, and a seaman is a sailor: said together they make the sound heard

explanation.surface: A merchant found in a dump, so says a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' signals that HOLE + SAILOR, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler is a trader who sells goods in bulk to shops rather than to the public.

clue.text: Influence of European currency leading to English anger

parts.note: the lev is the currency of Bulgaria
rage is fury or anger

explanation.surface: A sense that a foreign currency's power is making the English furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The lev is Bulgaria's money unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is power to sway outcomes, the extra force a lever gives.

clue.text: Individual person taking chance as criminal accomplice?

parts.note: A means one, a single individual
a better is someone who places a bet, taking a gamble

explanation.surface: A gambler is cast as a crook's partner in crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling is abettor; the question mark admits this variant.
explanation.definitionFit: An abetter assists or encourages someone committing a crime, an accessory.

clue.text: Plant Cockney poet found outside hotel

indicators.note: found outside means placed around, so the poet name wraps the hotel letter

parts.note: Horace with the aitch dropped, as a Cockney speaker would say it
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Cockney rhymester discovered growing a plant outside a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys (London East Enders) traditionally drop their aitches, so Horace becomes 'ORACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Orache is a leafy herb of the goosefoot family, sometimes eaten like spinach.

clue.text: To carry on pulling

parts.note: to wage a war or campaign is to carry it on

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep going with a tug.
explanation.definitionFit: Towage is the act of towing, hauling a vessel or vehicle, or the fee for it.

clue.text: Spooner's ruled out eternal punishment? That strikes a note

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds here change places

parts.note: something banned is ruled out
hell is the place of everlasting punishment

explanation.surface: Damnation forever is forbidden, and that hits the right note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' swaps the first sounds of BANNED HELL, which spoken gives the answer; the spelling settles on the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbell is a small bell rung by hand, each one sounding a single musical pitch.

clue.text: Arrangements for those appearing as actors and as imitators possibly

definitions.text: Arrangements for those appearing as actors

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might be arranged in another way, an anagram

explanation.surface: Plans for people performing on stage, whether as actors or as mimics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AND AS IMITATORS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatisation adapts a story into a script for performers to play.

clue.text: Agent was untruthful about wicked act being done again

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, acts as an agent

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for lying surrounds the rearranged letters

parts.note: lied means told untruths

indicators.note: wicked suggests twisted or perverse, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A rep fibbed about a sinful deed happening a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' is the anagram signal on 'act', not a description of it; 'about' places the result inside the word for lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Replicated means copied or repeated, carried out again exactly.

clue.text: Shrub beginning to languish unfortunately when growing up

indicators.note: in a down entry, growing up means reading from the bottom upwards
the beginning letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: A bush starts to droop, sadly, as it grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing up' reverses LALAS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Salal is an evergreen shrub of western North America, related to heather.

clue.text: Stone that's egg-shaped, soft but not very

indicators.note: but not says one letter is put in where another is taken away

parts.note: oval means egg-shaped
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A gem that is rounded like an egg and only slightly soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' swaps V (very) in OVAL for P (soft).
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone with shifting rainbow colours.

clue.text: Select group head ignored with exciting part of school curriculum

indicators.note: ignoring the head means leaving off the first letter

parts.note: an elite is a select group
racy means lively or exciting

explanation.surface: An exclusive club, minus its leader, plus a thrilling part of what pupils study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head ignored' drops ELITE's first letter, giving LITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading and writing skills are taught as a core school subject.

clue.text: After setback high-level worker perhaps is fired up again

indicators.note: a setback sets something back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a tiler works on roofs, high up

explanation.surface: Having suffered a reverse, a senior employee gets enthused again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-level' suggests a senior executive, but it means literally high: a roofer.
explanation.definitionFit: Relit means set alight once more, as a fire or pipe.

clue.text: Religious writing's disseminated in tract

definitions.note: the definition is possessive, so it describes something belonging to the writing: an adjective

indicators.note: disseminated means scattered about, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Sacred texts are distributed in a pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disseminated' rearranges IN TRACT.
explanation.definitionFit: The tantras are Hindu and Buddhist scriptures, so tantric means relating to those texts.

clue.text: Robust address being heard

indicators.note: being heard means the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: to hail someone is to call out to them, to address them

explanation.surface: A strong speech gets a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' looks like a noun, but it is the verb to hail.
explanation.definitionFit: Hale means healthy and strong, as in hale and hearty.

clue.text: Like space mission with number spinning round in a trip nearly going wrong

indicators.note: in says the reversed number goes inside the scrambled letters
going wrong suggests letters in disorder, an anagram
spinning round turns the number backwards

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A space voyage almost goes awry, with numbers whirling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning round' reverses the number; 'in' puts it inside the 'going wrong' anagram of 'a trip nearly'. 'nearly' looks like a cut signal but is fodder whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission to Mars travels between planets, the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Take back hypocritical talk in lessons about religion

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject
cant is insincere, sanctimonious talk

explanation.surface: Withdraw the sanctimonious waffle in scripture classes.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a statement or belief formally.

clue.text: Gaudy temple set up with uninteresting foundation

indicators.note: foundation says this piece goes at the base of the down entry
in a down entry, set up means read upward, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
dry means dull and uninteresting

explanation.surface: A garish shrine is built on a dull base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foundation' places DRY beneath TAW (WAT reversed by 'set up') in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawdry means showy but cheap, vulgarly flashy.

clue.text: Scotland does this — it helps family with baby

parts.note: the word Scotland contains, or carries, the letters c-o-t

explanation.surface: A boast that Scotland is good to young families.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the solution as an instruction: S(COT)LAND carries COT.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable cot is a bag with handles for carrying an infant.

clue.text: Stuff right off lorry

indicators.note: off means taken away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: truck is the American word for a British lorry

explanation.surface: Goods dropping straight off the back of a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' is a verb: to cram in.
explanation.definitionFit: To tuck is to push or cram something in, as a shirt into trousers.

clue.text: Trees, a mathematical number in lines

indicators.note: in puts the letters inside the word for lines

parts.note: rows are lines
n stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A grove planted in neat lines, numbered by a mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowans are mountain ash trees with red berries.

clue.text: Man right to be elevated

indicators.note: in a down entry, elevated means lifted up, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A man ought to be promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil is a man's first name.

clue.text: Century by cricket side after chaps rolled over without dissent

indicators.note: after puts the reversed word before the rest
rolled over means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: men are chaps
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
the on side is a half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team's hundred won after the opposition rolled over, without protest.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on (leg) side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nem con, Latin nemine contradicente, means with no one objecting, unanimously.

clue.text: Provider of gourd needs to check one with external slash

indicators.note: having something external means being wrapped by it, so the slash word goes round the rest

parts.note: to slash is to cut
to curb is to check or restrain
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gourd grower must inspect a plant with a cut on its outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cucurbit is a plant of the gourd family, which includes squash and melon.
